description: Narrative findings from the xebench cross-engine benchmark, published as data so consumers render the lab's wording verbatim and never re-word a claim. Schema: data/findings.schema.json.

findings.headline: Correction: LiteRT-LM on NPU is not blocked upstream. It runs, but must be assembled by hand, and one published bundle gives wrong output
findings.deck: We previously said Google withholds the libraries LiteRT-LM needs to run on a Qualcomm NPU. That was wrong: they are published. Our app was not bundling the dispatch library, and the other library was in the LiteRT-LM repository all along. NPU and GPU both ran in our 2026-10-17 spikes, but neither is measured on this board yet.
claims: Correction (2026-10-17): this finding previously said that no third party could run LiteRT-LM on a Qualcomm NPU, because Google withholds two prebuilt bridge libraries (libLiteRtDispatch_Qualcomm.so, libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.so). That conclusion was wrong.

Both libraries are published. Google has attached per-architecture dispatch libraries (including Hexagon v73) to LiteRT GitHub releases since v2.0.0-alpha (2025-05). They are also on Google Maven as com.google.ai.edge.litert:litert-npu-runtime-qualcomm (2.3.0, published 2026-10-06). libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.so has been committed in the LiteRT-LM repository under prebuilt/android_arm64/ since 2025-12.

Our July 2026 NPU failure (SIGABRT: 'No dispatch library found' / 'No usable Dispatch runtime found') happened because our app did not bundle the published dispatch library. We had misattributed it to a missing Hexagon v73 skel.

In 2026-10-17 spikes, Gemma 3 1B ran on the NPU of a Galaxy S23 (Snapdragon SM8550, Hexagon v73) and a POCO F8 Ultra (SM8850, Hexagon v81). The stack was litertlm-android 0.18.0, litert-npu-runtime-qualcomm 2.3.0, QAIRT 2.50.0.260828 (public download) and <uses-native-library> manifest declarations. It also ran with our July version, LiteRT-LM 0.14.0, using Google's prebuilt dispatch library from the LiteRT v2.1.6 release (2026-07-02).

The remaining friction is integration. The integrator assembles four artifacts by hand, and the dispatch library's ABI must match the LITERT_REF of the LiteRT-LM release. A mismatch logs 'Unsupported dispatch runtime version'. On LiteRT-LM 0.14.0 that is a native abort, and on 0.18.0 the Kotlin API reports only a generic 'Failed to create engine'.

The remaining upstream problem is correctness. On the Galaxy S23, Google's published SM8550 Gemma 3 1B NPU bundle (built with QAIRT 2.34.0) produces degenerate output for prompts longer than one 128-token prefill chunk (LiteRT-LM #3508). The SM8850 bundle (QAIRT 2.44) passed our three-prompt output check on the F8 Ultra, and CPU and GPU output is correct on both phones.
These were single-run spikes, not benchmark rows. This board does not yet publish any LiteRT-LM NPU measurement.

findings.resolution: LiteRT-LM NPU rows will appear here once they pass an output-correctness check. The S23 stays off the board until the SM8550 bundle bug (LiteRT-LM #3508) is fixed or a correct bundle is published.

findings.headline: With llama.rn 0.12.4 on a POCO F8 Ultra, llama.cpp's Hexagon backend gave wrong output; with 0.13.0-rc.7, Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B output was correct. The 0.12.4-era board row stays failed
findings.deck: On a POCO F8 Ultra, our output-correctness gate caught llama.cpp's Hexagon backend producing wrong output with llama.rn 0.12.4. A re-check with llama.rn 0.13.0-rc.7 gave correct output for Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B. The board's only llama.cpp NPU row comes from a 0.12.4-era build and was never output-checked, so it stays marked failed. The next measurement will be a separate Q4_K_M row (the pinned reference model).
claims: On 2026-10-17 we re-ran llama.cpp's Hexagon backend (HTP0) on a POCO F8 Ultra (Snapdragon SM8850, Hexagon v81) with llama.rn 0.12.4. That is the version our harness locks, and the one it locked when the board row was measured (the July build's own version was not recorded). Each Hexagon run was gated against llama.cpp on CPU with the same model file.

With llama.rn 0.12.4, Llama 3.2 1B (Q4_K_M and Q4_0) answered the short prompt (about 20 tokens) correctly. Every tested prompt longer than about 128 tokens, including the ~460-token measured prompt, degenerated into repeated fragments such as 'which, which, which …' and 'ususus…'.
With llama.rn 0.12.4, Gemma 3 1B (Q4_0) failed even the short prompt, producing a repeated token.
llama.cpp on CPU, using the same Llama 3.2 1B Q4_K_M file, answered every answer probe correctly.

With llama.rn 0.13.0-rc.7, on the same phone and configuration (4 repetitions per Hexagon run), the Hexagon output for Llama 3.2 1B was correct. Q4_K_M passed all four answer probes, the same as its CPU reference. Its output on the ~460-token measured prompt is not identical to the CPU output; the gate checks the answer probes, not identical output. Q4_0 passed the same probes as its CPU reference, which itself misses one long-fact probe on CPU (a model-quality miss), so that gate is unverified rather than wrong. Evidence bundle 20009fec0a56fe4bcb2b0046a2e160e3fca5c9263de1fef8a364dc62674ca210 (4 sessions; bundle integrity verified; the Q4_K_M CPU reference stopped at 3 of 4 repetitions on a readiness timeout, after its correctness gate had passed).

With llama.rn 0.13.0-rc.7 on the same phone, the Hexagon output for Gemma 3 1B (QAT Q4_0 GGUF) was correct: every probe passed, including the short probe that failed with 0.12.4 (10 repetitions; the engine confirmed HTP0; comparison valid against the CPU reference). Evidence bundle beb9a67ced8709bf195a64d048be0d8529505f5b76e24ee612de2d8867046bd2 (3 sessions; bundle integrity verified).

The board's only llama.cpp NPU row (F8 Ultra, Llama 3.2 1B, Q4_0) was measured on a ~512-token prompt with no output check, by a 0.12.4-era build. It stays marked 'failed': its output was never checked, and a speed measured while the output may be wrong says nothing about correct inference. Its numbers are kept for the record. The next measurement will be a separate Q4_K_M row (the pinned reference model); this Q4_0 row stays failed.
Earlier xebench docs called this backend functional and said it lost to the CPU on this phone. Both statements are withdrawn.
These results cover llama.rn 0.12.4 and 0.13.0-rc.7 on this phone with these models. They are not a claim about other versions, phones or models. No 0.13.0-rc.7 speed is published here yet.
